CSCO.rationale: Cisco shows solid fundamental health with accelerating revenue and EPS growth (Q2 FY2026 revenue +9.7% YoY, EPS +31.1% YoY), strong gross margins (~65%), and a healthy balance sheet (debt-to-equity 0.52). The company is executing a successful software/subscription transformation post-Splunk, with ARR approaching $30B and software exceeding 50% of revenue. However, operating cash flow declined 18.7% YoY in Q2, and the stock has rallied significantly (+19.2% in the past quarter) pushing the P/E to 31.9x — the top of its 12-month range (24.5–33.5x). At this valuation, the stock is no longer cheap relative to its own history, which caps upside. The upcoming Q3 earnings report (analysts expect $0.86 EPS, +10.3% YoY) provides a near-term catalyst, and the company has beaten estimates consistently.
